segments.text: Gummy stretches a rubber band and lets go.
It snaps right back to its original length.
Clay stays stretched once you pull it,
but a rubber band keeps pulling itself back.
Inside, it's packed with long, thin, thread-like molecules.
Normally those threads sit tangled up, like a ball of yarn.
Pulling stretches those tangled threads straight.
Let go, and they want to tangle up again.
That's the threads bunching back together.
That's why the rubber band shrinks back.
